title: Verify native account deletion cannot race away the last active admin
classification: No new implementation defect reproduced. The native deletion adapter serializes account mutations with the shared transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock and revalidates the actor after lock acquisition.

scenario.actors: Two active admin accounts, each requesting deletion of the other at the same barrier.
scenario.expected: One transaction deletes its target; the other sees its actor is no longer active and is denied. Exactly one active admin remains.

verification.result: passed: 3 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.database: Fresh uniquely named PostgreSQL test database upgraded from the Alembic baseline through d6e7f8a9b0c1.
verification.cleanup: The disposable database was dropped after the passing run.
verification.coverage: The new test invokes AdminUserMutationData.delete concurrently from separate thread-scoped SQLAlchemy sessions; it verifies one successful deletion, one forbidden inactive-actor result, and one remaining active admin. Existing legacy deactivation race and NULL-state admin regressions also pass.

limits: This tests the native mutation data adapter and PostgreSQL transaction lock, not a full ASGI authentication/CSRF request journey.
P2-10 failure injection at every transaction stage, restart/repeat convergence, and the broader P2-09 tabletop remain open.
